newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ overseas debt rises 2.4 percent in Dec qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ overseas debt rises 2.4 percent in Dec qtr.

text.p: New Zealand's total overseas debt rose NZ$1.9 billion, or 2.4 percent, in the December quarter, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said on Tuesday.
The $79.8 billion total overseas debt at December 31 was $5.3 billion, or 7.1 percent, higher than the year-ago figure.
"The December 1996 quarter rise in total overseas debt was caused by net new borrowings of $2.4 billion, offset partly by exchange rate gains estimated at $0.5 billion," SNZ said.
Official government sector overseas debt fell $0.3 billion to $22.3 billion in the quarter as the official sector continued to repay foreign currency debt.

"However, ongoing increases in foreign holdings of New Zealand dollar denominated government securities has resulted in official sector overseas debt remaining generally flat over the past two years," SNZ said.

Corporate sector overseas debt rose $2.2 billion in the December quarter to $57.5 billion. Major influences were rises in corporate sector overseas loans, bills and bonds, offset by a fall in foreign currency deposits from overseas residents in New Zealand financial institutions.

New Zealand's total overseas debt held as loans, and bills and bonds, rose $2.6 billion and $0.6 billion respectively in the quarter, offset partly by a $1.7 billion fall in overseas deposits in New Zealand financial institutions.
SNZ said overseas loans had been variable but generally rising over the last three years, while bills and bonds had been in general decline due to the official sector's debt repayment.
New Zealand's overseas debt to GDP ratio at December 31 was 85.0 percent, against 84.6 percent at September 30 and 83.6 percent at December 31 1995.
